parts.title: Word List
parts.content:
Detailed Meanings

😎
adorn[ado:rn]v.
To adorn something means to make it more beautiful by decorating it.
→ Small glass beads adorned the vase.
😎
bliss[blis]n.
Bliss is a state of complete happiness.
→ Every time he sees his girlfriend, he feels a sense of bliss.
😎
butler[bAtlar]n.
A butler is the most important male servant in a wealthy house.
→ Whenever he needed something, he rang a bell, and the butler appeared.
😎
cramp[kraemp]n.
A cramp is a strong pain caused by a muscle after a lot of physical use.
→ After the marathon, Jenny got a terrible cramp in her calf muscle.
😎
dilapidated[dileepadeitid]adj.
When a building is dilapidated, it is old and in bad condition.
→ Paint peeled off of the old dilapidated apartment building.
😎
evoke[ivouk]v.
To evoke a memory or emotion means to make it occur.
→ The picture evoked memories of when grandmother was a girl.
😎
farewell[fearwel]n.
A farewell is an instance of saying goodbye or a way to say it.
→ She got on the plane after we said our farewells.
😎
faucet[fo:sit]n.
A faucet is a device that controls the flow of a liquid or gas.
→ Turn off the faucet when you are done brushing your teeth.
😎
filth[file]n.
Filth is a large amount of dirt or dirty things that disgust you.
→ There was tons of filth and trash on the shore of the river.
😎
flaw[flo]n.
A flaw is a mistake in something that causes it to be less effective or correct.
→ We discovered a major flaw in the metal chain.
😎
grin[grin]v.
To grin means to smile broadly.
→ That joke makes me grin every time I hear it.
😎
housekeeping[hauski:pir)]n.
Housekeeping is the maintenance of a house or an establishment like a hotel.
→ Housekeeping is not much fun, but it has to be done.
😎
mound[maund]n.
A mound of something is a large pile of it.
→ There was a mound of clothes on the messy teenager’s floor.
😎
numb[nAm]adj.
When a body part is numb, it does not have any feeling.
→ After holding my hand under the icy water, my fingers went numb.
😎
reckless[reklis]adj.
When people are reckless, they act in an unsafe way.
→ The reckless driver posed a threat to everyone else on the road.
😎
slate[sleit]n.
Slate is a dark grey rock that can easily be split into layers.
→ The roof of the church was made of slate.
😎
stool[stu:l]n.
A stool is a seat with legs but no support for a person’s arms and back.
→ I don’t find stools very comfortable to sit on.
😎
testament[testament]n.
A testament to something shows that it exists or is true.
→ The beautiful performance was a testament to the singer’s natural talents.
😎
timber[timber]n.
Timber is wood that is used for building houses and making furniture.
→ Trees in this area are grown specifically to be used for timber.
😎
valve[vaelv]n.
A valve is a device attached to a pipe that controls the flow of liquid or air.
→ The mechanic removed the dirt to clear the engine valve.

sections.title: Exercise 1: Write a word that is similar in meaning to the underlined part.

questions.content:
The large pile of dirt covered most of the backyard. [ 1 ]

Please call for the most important male servant. [ 2 ]

I don’t think we have enough wood used for building furniture to complete the project. [ 3 ]

The playful puppy made the baby smile broadly. [ 4 ]

We’ll have to install a new device that attaches to a tube to control the flow of liquid. [ 5 ]

I got a small muscle pain in my leg after having a long workout at the gym. [ 6 ]

To reach the TV, the young girl stood on the seat with legs but no arm support. [ 7 ]

A high examination score is a proof of the existence of good studying skills. [ 8 ]

The man became worried when his arm was without feeling. [ 9 ]

He was hired to repair the house that had become old and in bad condition. [ 10 ]
questions.explanation: mound (n): a large pile of something.
butler (n): the most important male servant in a wealthy house.
timber (n): wood that is used for building houses and making furniture.
grin (v): to smile broadly.
valve (n): a device attached to a pipe that controls the flow of liquid or air.
cramp (n): a strong pain caused by a muscle after a lot of physical use.
stool (n): a seat with legs but no support for a person’s arms and back.
testament (n): a testament to something shows that it exists or is true.
numb (adj): when a body part does not have any feeling.
dilapidated (adj): old and in bad condition.

sections.title: Exercise 2: Write C if the italicized word is used correctly. Write I if the word is used incorrectly.

questions.content: The scientist’s theory was full of flaws. There was no way it could work.
questions.explanation: Flaw means a mistake in something that causes it to be less effective or correct.

questions.content: The butler catered to the old man’s every need.
questions.explanation: Butler means the most important male servant in a wealthy house.

questions.content: I hope we do not have to say farewells to the bus to school.
questions.explanation: Farewell means goodbye, usually to people, not to objects like a bus.

questions.content: The teacher was proud of the filth her students achieved in class.
questions.explanation: Filth is a large amount of dirt or dirty things that disgust you. It is not something to be proud of.

questions.content: After the initial pain of dropping the hammer on my toe, it went numb.
questions.explanation: Numb means a body part does not have any feeling.

questions.content: He was not looking forward to cleaning the huge mound of dirty dishes in the sink.
questions.explanation: Mound means a large pile of something.

questions.content: The scared child felt bliss and cried for his mother.
questions.explanation: Bliss is a state of complete happiness, which contradicts being scared and crying.

questions.content: Huge stained-glass windows adorn the new church.
questions.explanation: Adorn means to make it more beautiful by decorating it.

questions.content: Fossil evidence is a testament to the immense size of dinosaurs.
questions.explanation: Testament means proof that something exists or is true.

questions.content: The reckless climber took every precaution to insure a safe climb.
questions.explanation: Reckless means acting in an unsafe way, which contradicts taking every precaution.

parts.title: Comprehensive Reading
parts.content:
The Butler

Greta was an elderly lady who lived alone in a huge, dilapidated mansion. The mansion was in terrible condition. It was covered with filth, and most of the furniture was broken. Plus, the kitchen sink leaked water all over the floor. Greta was too old to do housekeeping and repairs herself, so she hired a butler named Gordon.

Gordon was a young, muscular man. His muscles were a testament to his strong work ethic. He believed that if he worked hard, great things would happen for him. On his first day, he worked for hours cleaning and making repairs. He swept up mounds of dirt. He tightened the valve underneath the kitchen faucet to stop the leak. He even bought timber to build new stools for the kitchen. He worked so hard that his fingers went numb, and he got cramps in his shoulders.

Gordon worked hard every day. Even when tasks were boring, he was never reckless. He made sure there were no flaws in his work. Gordon was worried, however, that Greta wasn’t pleased. She never expressed thanks or said that he did a good job. The lack of appreciation evoked unhappy feelings in Gordon. He even thought about quitting. But he decided the right thing to do was to keep working hard.

One day, while Gordon was sweeping, Greta said, “Gordon! I have a surprise for you!” He went to Greta’s room and saw a beautiful slate statue. It looked just like him! It was adorned with a banner that read: “Welcome home.”

Greta said, “You’ve made this ugly old mansion look new again. I’m so thankful for your hard work that I want you to have it. I’ll move into a smaller house.”

He grinned and gave Greta a big hug. He said, “I’m in bliss! My hard work really paid off!”

The two said their farewells, and Gordon spent the afternoon admiring his beautiful new home.

sections.title: Part A: Mark each statement T for true or F for false.

questions.content: The dilapidated mansion was covered in filth.
questions.explanation: Đáp án là Đúng (T). Ngay ở đoạn đầu, bài đọc có mô tả về căn biệt thự: "The mansion was in terrible condition. It was covered with filth" (Dinh thự ở trong tình trạng tồi tệ. Nó bị bao phủ bởi bụi bẩn).

questions.content: Gordon’s muscles were a testament to his flaws.
questions.explanation: Đáp án là Sai (F). Ở đoạn hai viết: "His muscles were a testament to his strong work ethic" (Cơ bắp của anh là minh chứng cho tinh thần làm việc hăng say của anh), chứ không phải là minh chứng cho những khuyết điểm (flaws).

questions.content: Gordon was never reckless even when tasks were boring.
questions.explanation: Đáp án là Đúng (T). Trong đoạn ba có câu xác nhận rõ ràng: "Even when tasks were boring, he was never reckless" (Ngay cả khi công việc có nhàm chán, anh ấy cũng không bao giờ làm việc cẩu thả/thiếu thận trọng).

questions.content: The mound of dirt evoked unhappy feelings in Gordon.
questions.explanation: Đáp án là Sai (F). Theo đoạn ba, thứ gợi lên cảm giác buồn bã ở Gordon là do Greta không thể hiện sự trân trọng: "The lack of appreciation evoked unhappy feelings in Gordon" (Sự thiếu trân trọng đã gợi lên những cảm xúc không vui ở Gordon), chứ không phải vì đống bụi bẩn.

questions.content: Gordon tightened the valve under the kitchen faucet and bought timber to build stools.
questions.explanation: Đáp án là Đúng (T). Đoạn hai liệt kê các việc anh làm: "He tightened the valve underneath the kitchen faucet to stop the leak. He even bought timber to build new stools for the kitchen."

questions.content: Why did Greta hire a butler to do the housekeeping and repairs?
options: She didn't know how to do them.
Greta was too old to do housekeeping and repairs herself.
She was too busy with her job.
She had a lot of money to spend.
questions.explanation: Đáp án đúng là B. Cuối đoạn một giải thích lý do bà Greta phải thuê quản gia: "Greta was too old to do housekeeping and repairs herself, so she hired a butler named Gordon." (Greta đã quá già để tự mình làm công việc dọn dẹp nhà cửa và sửa chữa, vì vậy bà đã thuê một quản gia tên là Gordon).

questions.content: Why did Gordon’s shoulders get cramps and his fingers become numb?
questions.explanation: Đáp án đúng là C. Ở đoạn hai miêu tả quá trình làm việc chăm chỉ liên tục của anh, dẫn đến kết quả: "He worked so hard that his fingers went numb, and he got cramps in his shoulders." (Anh ấy làm việc chăm chỉ đến nỗi các ngón tay trở nên tê dại, và anh bị chuột rút ở vai).

questions.content: What was written on the banner that adorned the slate statue?
questions.explanation: Đáp án đúng là A. Ở đoạn bốn có mô tả chi tiết bức tượng: "It was adorned with a banner that read: 'Welcome home.'" (Nó được trang trí với một dải ruy băng có dòng chữ: 'Chào mừng về nhà.').

questions.content: What did Gordon say when he grinned and felt bliss?
questions.explanation: Đáp án đúng là B. Đoạn sáu thuật lại lời Gordon nói khi anh cười rạng rỡ và cảm thấy vô cùng sung sướng: "He said, 'I’m in bliss! My hard work really paid off!'" (Anh ấy nói: 'Tôi đang rất hạnh phúc! Sự chăm chỉ của tôi thực sự đã được đền đáp!').

questions.content: What happened after Greta and Gordon said their farewells?
options: Gordon got a cramp in his leg.
Gordon spent the afternoon admiring his beautiful new home.
Greta went to buy more slate.
questions.explanation: Đáp án đúng là C. Câu cuối cùng của bài đọc cho biết việc diễn ra sau đó: "The two said their farewells, and Gordon spent the afternoon admiring his beautiful new home." (Hai người nói lời tạm biệt, và Gordon dành cả buổi chiều để chiêm ngưỡng ngôi nhà mới tuyệt đẹp của mình).
